scenarios.title: Email provider outage
scenarios.description: The primary email provider returns errors for an hour.
probes: What happens to messages already in flight and those arriving during the outage?
Do you fail over to another provider, and how do you avoid duplicate sends?
How large does the queue grow and what protects other channels?

scenarios.title: Campaign floods the system
scenarios.description: A marketing campaign enqueues tens of millions of messages while one-time passcodes are being requested.
probes: How do passcodes keep their latency target?
Where is the bottleneck: queue, workers, provider limits, or the database?
How can the campaign be paused or cancelled?

scenarios.title: Retry loop amplifies traffic
scenarios.description: A provider slows down; timeouts trigger retries from every worker, increasing load further.
probes: How do backoff, jitter, and circuit breakers interact in your design?
How do you tell a retryable error from a permanent one?
What stops duplicates when a timed-out request actually succeeded?

scenarios.title: Consumer group falls behind
scenarios.description: Workers for one channel cannot keep up and queue lag grows steadily.
probes: How do you detect lag and what triggers scaling or load shedding?
How are stale notifications, such as an expired passcode, handled once they are finally processed?
How do poison messages avoid blocking a partition?

scenarios.title: Opt-out race
scenarios.description: A user unsubscribes just after a large campaign has been enqueued.
triggers: Preference change while messages are queued
probes: At what point is the preference checked?
How stale can the preference cache be, and is that legally acceptable?
How do you prove to an auditor that the user was not contacted?
